# Pitex 1.0.7

This release fixes opening very large folders, such as Downloads, which could
freeze Ubuntu, and makes folders outside a Git repository open faster.

## Changes

- Opening a folder now scans a bounded part of it: at most 50,000 names and
  2,000 directories, keeping up to 2,000 source files and 2,000 figures. The
  scan skips `node_modules`, `venv` and `__pycache__`, stays on the opened
  filesystem and stops at directory cycles. When the list is partial, the
  sidebar says so. A folder too large to contain any source file within these
  limits is refused with "This folder is too large to open."
- Text files larger than 32 MiB and preview PDFs larger than 50 MiB are no
  longer read whole into memory.
- Git status lists a wholly untracked directory as one entry instead of every
  file inside it, and stops if the listing exceeds 4 MiB. Opening a folder
  inside a large untracked tree is no longer slow.
- The same limits apply on macOS, Ubuntu and Windows.

## Install

Pitex 1.0.0 through 1.0.6 update to 1.0.7 from Settings or, with automatic
installation enabled, at launch. For Homebrew installations, run
`brew update` and `brew upgrade --cask pitex`.

Builds from the earlier 2.x line do not update automatically; install 1.0.7
from the downloads below. Pitex Nightly continues to use its separate
update channel.

## Downloads

Downloads include the macOS ARM64 DMG, Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 AMD64 DEBs,
Windows AMD64 installer and portable ZIP, the Ubuntu installer, and
SHA256SUMS.
Windows remains beta.
